title: Induced subgraph counts determine component counts of disconnected graphs
statement_en: If G and H on n vertices are both disconnected and have the same number of induced copies of every graph on fewer than n vertices, then for every connected graph F they have the same number of connected components isomorphic to F (triangular solve: induced connected copies lie inside one component, all components have fewer than n vertices).
statement_lean: ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G H : SimpleGraph (Fin n), ¬ G.Connected → ¬ H.Connected → (∀ k : ℕ, k < n → ∀ F : SimpleGraph (Fin k), {S : Finset (Fin n) | Nonempty (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n)) ≃g F)}.ncard = {S : Finset (Fin n) | Nonempty (H.induce (S : Set (Fin n)) ≃g F)}.ncard) → ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ F : SimpleGraph (Fin k), F.Connected → {c : G.ConnectedComponent | Nonempty (G.induce c.supp ≃g F)}.ncard = {c : H.ConnectedComponent | Nonempty (H.induce c.supp ≃g F)}.ncard
author: reducer
